text:
elen: Observed a regression after the kernel-selector tweak — Llama2-13B hosted lane shows ~8-12% p50/p95 latency bump across steady traffic. root cause unclear, posting initial traces and config I used.

jay: Can you paste the flamegraph and the kernel selection log? also which pool (gpu type)?

elen: Pool is g5-large (prod-dedicated). Flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/dev/flame/2734509999 (shortlink). Key snippet from runtime logs: 

```
[2026-03-18 09:12:34] kernel-selector: matched fused_matmul_opt for llama2-13b.v3 -> loading
[2026-03-18 09:12:34] fallback: kernel mismatch -> using matmul_generic (slowpath)
[2026-03-18 09:12:34] batcher: batch size avg 3.1 -> expected 4.7
```

elen: perf-bot profile attached below shows hotspots in `kv_cache::read_kv_block` and `matmul_generic::run`. p95 latency delta mostly when seq_len > 512 and chat template prefix present.

perf-bot: Automated run 2734509999-results: baseline vs current -> p50 +9%, p95 +11%, tokens/sec -7%. Top traces: kernel fallback (matmul_generic), small-batch overhead, extra memcpy on KV spill.

nora: Two quick checks: 1) Is rope_theta forced to a different default in the model config? we had a change that overrides RoPE scaling for some llama2 variants which can change rotary embedding tiling and head partitioning -> can force non-fused kernel. 2) Are we accidentally zeroing the KV cache prefix so batcher reduces batching effectiveness for chat templates?

elen: Good call. Current model config excerpt: 
```
model: llama2-13b.v3
hidden_size: "5120"
num_heads: "40"
rope_theta: "auto"  # used to be 10000.0 explicit in v2 configs
norm: "rmsnorm"
activation: "silu"
kernel_autoselect: "true"
```

elen: When `rope_theta: auto` we run runtime heuristics that recompute rotary frequencies; suspect that changed the head->kv layout at compile time and invalidated `fused_matmul` pattern matching.

jay: If fused kernel pattern matching is based on (heads, head_dim, dtype, stride) then a subtle stride change can flip to `matmul_generic`. Can you dump the kernel fingerprint (we log it with `--kernel-fingerprint`)?

sam: Also double-check batcher heuristics: `min_batch_size_for_fused=4` and with chat-template caching disabled we saw avg batch 3.1 -> fusion not kicked in. Quick experiment: set `min_batch_size_for_fused=2` on a canary and measure. Might hide underlying regression but helps triage.

nora: Don't forget KV eviction policy: we recently changed `kv_spill_threshold` from 8k tokens to 6k tokens in the same deploy group. Lower threshold increases evictions and memcpy overhead. If the same requests hit eviction path, you see memcpys in hot path.

elen: Running two micro-experiments now: (A) pin `rope_theta: 10000.0` and disable `kernel_autoselect` (force fused_matmul), (B) set `min_batch_size_for_fused=2` + restore kv_spill_threshold to 8k. I'll post numbers in ~20m.

perf-bot: Queued experiments: exp-273450A, exp-273450B. ETA ~18m.

jay: If A recovers p95 -> it's kernel-fingerprint/layout change. If B recovers -> batching/eviction is main. If neither -> check RMSNorm -> SiLU codepath: we had a micro-optimization that fused rmsnorm+silu into a single kernel for llamas with head_dim % 32 == 0, but if head_dim changes due to rope tiling, fusion drops out.

sam: One more small test: run a profiler with `--simulate-chat-prefix true` vs false. Chat templates can make effective prefix length jump and change KV cache reuse ratio.

elen: results: exp-273450A (pin rope + force fused) -> p50 -4%, p95 -9% vs current; tokens/sec +6%. exp-273450B (lowered min_batch_size) -> p50 -2%, p95 -3%. So A gives the biggest win.

nora: That matches kernel-fingerprint hypothesis. We should revert `rope_theta: auto` behavior for llama2 family and add a targeted unit test asserting kernel fingerprint stability for common head/hidden combos.

elen: Agreed. Plan: revert auto-rope change in next canary, add an assertion in model-onboard tests (compare `--kernel-fingerprint` against baseline), and add a diagnostic metric exposed to metrics (kernel-selection fallback count).

jay: SGTM. I'll prep the canary patch for runtime to disable auto-rope for lambdas in the model catalog, and also add a watch on `kernel_fallback_count`.

sam: I'll handle batcher tweak as stopgap (lower threshold) but add a note: we shouldn't rely on that for perf correctness.

elen: thanks all. filing a short postmortem note after we revert. :thumbsup:

sam: nice find. TLDR: rope_theta auto led to changed stride/head tiling -> kernel pattern mismatch -> fallback to matmul_generic -> latency spike.

perf-bot: Experiment summary stored at https://perf.redwood/exp/273450_summary (auto-uploaded).
